newsitem.title: cambodia: Sihanouk vows not to run in 1998 elections.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk vows not to run in 1998 elections.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has vowed he will not abdicate to run in general elections due next year but says he is unhappy on the throne.
"I will never stand in these legislative elections in 1998," Sihanouk said in a written interview conducted by his cabinet and released by the palace on Wednesday.
However the 74-year-old monarch added: "I have never found myself at ease as king."
Sihanouk left for China on Wednesday for an eye operation and a medical check-up.
He leaves at a time of heightened tensions between the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and the royalist FUNCINPEC party, which formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Some analysts believe the CPP and its leader, co-premier Hun Sen, fear the king might quit to lead a royalist party to victory at the polls on the back of his grass roots popularity.
The king's son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, leads FUNCINPEC.
Sihanouk said in the interview he was "seriously thinking of abdicating" but he added it would not be before the year 2000 to reassure those who feared he would run in next year's elections.

Sihanouk also denied he would start a new political party or seek to revive the Sangkum Reastr Niyum (SRN), a mass political organisation he founded upon abdicating for the first time in 1955 to give him greater political freedom.
The constitution that restored Sihanouk to the throne in 1993 provides for a monarch who reigns but does not rule.
He claimed there was a growing republican and anti-Sihanouk movement that had infiltrated the major parties and gained influential and important posts. He did not mention any names.
Newspapers regarded as supporters of the CPP or pro-republican have launched periodic attacks on the king and his wife.

Sihanouk flew to Beijing early on Wednesday and a royal palace official said he was going for a regular medical check-up and was likely to be away for a month. The king has said he will have a cataract operation on his right eye.
The king has managed to beat cancer but suffers from a range of other ailments, including arterio-sclerosis and diabetes.
